newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Volatility dip will be short.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Volatility dip will be short.

text.p: Volatility in major U.S. stock options subsided a bit Friday ahead of the weekend in quiet action, but traders said it would most likely pick up again next week.
"They'll probably take volatility in after next week, but until then it's going to be a roller-coaster ride," said one S&P 500 futures-options trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange.
"You're going to have a lot of (volatility) come in because of weekend time decay," he said. But he added some calendar spreads were being bid up, keeping volatility firm.
The trader said volatility in front-month S&P 500 futures-options was ranging from about 18.9 to 19.2.
"Volatility's been relatively high for the last couple of days," he said.
Traders said the market's extreme choppiness this week has helped to keep volatilities pumped up.
Volatilities were also easing at the Chicago Board Options Exchange, where the volatility index, calculated from select S&P 100 index options, reached a two-month high Wednesday.
The VIX was down 0.87, or about 3.65 percent, at 23.10.
Jerry Hegarty, an options analyst at Thomson Financial Services, said in a report that the week after an expiration typically sees volatility ease.
"I think volatility will subside somewhat today and the range for the S&P 500 futures will be between 10 and 12 points," he said. "Next week should be very active."
At about 1200 CDT/1700 GMT, September S&P 500 futures were up 6.75 at 901. They had traded between 895.30 and 902 so far.
The 30-stock Dow industrial average was ahead 81 points at 7,735, its best level of the day.
Jay Shartsis, head of options trading at R.F. Lafferty & Co, said the market's high volatility could be a sign of an impending correction.
"Extreme volatility appears in tops," he said, adding that some sentiment measures had reached extremely bullish levels.
"So it's entirely possible the market is about to give back about one-third of its huge advance of about 1,400 points" on the Dow, he said.
The trader noted that lower lows have been posted for two straight sessions in S&P 500 futures, a negative technical development.
"I don't think we'll make a lower low today but I think they're going to try to push it down for a correction next week," he said. "I think you'd better watch the downside."
Next week's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, U.S. purchasing managers data and June U.S. employment report will be the triggers for an increase in volatility, dealers said.
Trading so far on Friday was relatively slow despite the solid gains, traders said.
"I think it's Saturday here on the floor," the trader at the CME said.
